stories.title: Locals launch campaign to buy ancient wood
summary: Locals have a year to raise the money needed to buy Ruscombe Wood near Stroud.

stories.title: House martin artificial nests scheme set to expand
summary: The artificial nests are more robust than the endangered migratory birds' own mud creations.

stories.title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change
summary: The global campaign to restore the "soggy secret weapon" that can combat against climate change.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain
summary: A surprising discovery suggests that some early signs of Alzheimer’s disease may begin outside the brain.

Using miniature laboratory systems made from human cells, scientists found that genetic mutations associated with inherited Alzheimer’s can disrupt nerve-to-muscle connections without any involvement from the brain or spinal cord.
This could help explain why some patients experience changes in balance, walking, and coordination long before memory problems develop.

stories.title: After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay
summary: CERN scientists have finally found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it happens only once in roughly 10 billion decays, ending a search spanning more than 40 years.
The breakthrough could help physicists uncover hidden particles and forces that lie beyond the reach of today's most powerful accelerators.

stories.title: Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee
summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden gut-to-brain dopamine pathway that helps explain why bitter coffee and other initially unpleasant flavors can become favorites over time.
The discovery reveals how the brain learns to crave certain foods and could eventually lead to new ways of reshaping eating habits and food preferences.

stories.title: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
summary: The vandalism of a nearby home heating oil tank resulted in the death of 13 birds from the park.

stories.title: A quantum breakthrough makes light behave like both a solid and a liquid
summary: Scientists have observed a bizarre quantum state of matter that combines the structure of a crystal with the frictionless flow of a liquid, all at room temperature.
The breakthrough overturns a major practical limitation of exotic quantum experiments and could help bring powerful new light-based computing and sensing technologies closer to reality.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between acorns and lyme disease
summary: After more than 35 years of research, scientists have uncovered surprising clues about what really drives Lyme disease risk.
Contrary to longstanding assumptions, deer populations appear less important than mice, which can fuel a 40% increase in tick numbers the following year.
Even acorn production can predict tick population surges two years in advance, while extreme temperatures may be far less deadly to ticks than scientists once believed.

stories.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
summary: A surprising new study from UCLA suggests that a naturally occurring molecule could help breast cancer survivors overcome the frustrating brain fog and exhaustion that can linger long after treatment ends.
Researchers found that women taking an oxaloacetate supplement for eight weeks experienced substantial improvements in memory, concentration, mental clarity, and fatigue.

stories.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
summary: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027.
Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.

stories.title: Scientists predict 2026 hottest year on record as climate talks begin
summary: Scientists are predictng this could be the hottest year on record as the COP31 climate summit opens.

stories.title: Print commissioned by Nasa uncovered for exhibition
summary: The Pop Art at Cartwright Hall exhibition tells the story of the British International Print Biennale.

stories.title: DNA on the Shroud of Turin reveals centuries of hidden secrets
summary: The Shroud of Turin, one of history's most mysterious religious artifacts, is yielding surprising new clues through DNA analysis.
Scientists have uncovered a complex mixture of biological traces that may reveal more about the cloth's past and the environments it encountered.
The findings offer a fresh scientific perspective on a centuries-old mystery that continues to spark fascination and debate.

stories.title: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon
summary: Scientists have discovered that the stickiness of underwater “marine snow” plays a surprisingly important role in how much carbon reaches the deep ocean.
Gooier particles resist bacterial breakdown and can transport more than six times as much carbon to the depths, revealing an unexpected connection between ocean slime and Earth's climate.

stories.title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse
summary: New figures suggest hazel dormice may be recovering after decades of decline, with warmer summers boosting survival.

stories.title: Scientists discover stunning new Amazon fish that may already be endangered
summary: Researchers have discovered a stunning new species of tiny orange-patterned fish in the Brazilian Amazon, but its survival may already be at risk.
Named Laimosemion laranja, the brilliantly colored killifish measures less than three centimeters long and was found in just three small forest pools.
Its extremely limited habitat is threatened by mining, deforestation, pollution, and expanding development.

stories.title: Scientists wipe out deadly brain tumors in every mouse tested with new cancer therapy
summary: Scientists at UC San Francisco have developed a powerful new cancer therapy that remains inactive until it reaches the brain, where it switches on to attack deadly tumors.

The engineered immune cells, called B-SYNC CAR-T cells, completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma (DMG), an aggressive childhood brain cancer that is almost always fatal within a year, in two mouse models.

stories.title: An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution
summary: A remarkable fossil discovery in Colombia is challenging how scientists understand major evolutionary changes in Earth's history.

Researchers uncovered an incredibly diverse ancient marine ecosystem where giant reptiles, sharks, and other creatures thrived as older evolutionary groups approached extinction and newer ones emerged.
They call this previously unrecognized pattern a "Biotic Inflection," suggesting that major transformations in life can occur without mass extinctions.

stories.title: Einstein's equations reveal how gravity could break, reconnect, and release energy
summary: More than a century after Einstein revolutionized our understanding of gravity, scientists have uncovered a surprising new phenomenon hidden within his equations.

Researchers at Columbia University and Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez have identified a theoretical process called "gravitational reconnection," in which structures within gravitational fields can break apart and reconnect, transferring energy into matter.
